0.original: Y'shtola wears a haunted expression, Emet-Selch's words having clearly found their mark.

48.original: The eldest and most powerful of primals... Gods. If that were Hydaelyn's origin, then what would that make─<hex:02100103>...No. No, I will not take the words of an Ascian on trust. It has to be a lie.

49.original: Thancred did tell me about primals...but I don't fully understand what all of this means.

50.original: 'Tis oft said truth is a matter of perspective. Yet upon <hex:021A020203>this<hex:021A020103> matter, there can be but one truth. I only pray it is not his.

51.original: <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>, you are returned! But...something troubles you. Is aught amiss?

52.original: What has happened to the sky!? I have never seen anything like it!

54.original: Though recent events plainly warrant further discussion, I think it best that we wait until Alphinaud and the others are present.

55.original: ...Emet-Selch included. How convenient that he should choose this moment to keep to the shadows.

56.original: Well...no matter. For the present, we should return to Fanow and make certain of the Eulmorans' withdrawal.

57.original: After that, Slitherbough. The Blessed are no doubt elated by what has become of the sky.

58.original: You are returned. And unharmed, I see.

59.original: Indeed. I am pleased to report that the Lightwarden is no more, thanks in large part to you.

60.original: That the death of a single sin eater should make such a difference...

61.original: As our numbers waned, so too did our hope that the ruins we have devoted our lives to guarding would ever find purpose.

62.original: Yet here you are, the allies for whom we have waited these many centuries. And with your arrival came the chance to pass on our legacy─the ancient wisdom of the empire.

63.original: That alone would have been reward enough... Never did we imagine it would serve to banish the Light that pervaded these woods.

64.original: On behalf of the Viis, our forebears, and the late emperor of Ronka, you have our deepest thanks.

65.original: It is we who should be thanking you. Our journey through the Qitana Ravel proved...most enlightening.

66.original: To be privy to such knowledge is an honor. One for which we never hoped...

67.original: Please, you need not be so humble!

68.original: We but do our duty as decreed by the late emperor. Would that he were still with us to express his gratitude in person.

69.original: But Sister, does this not mean our duty is fulfilled?

70.original: To our allies, perhaps, but the ruins cannot be left unguarded.

71.original: So long as we live here in these woods, the secrets of Ronka must not fall into the wrong hands.

73.original: No, we escorted him back to Slitherbough shortly after you set out.

74.original: If you would return to the Night's Blessed, we will not keep you any longer. I suspect they would be glad of your company.

75.original: Thank you, Almet. I look forward to a day when we might share a more leisurely visit to the ruins of Ronka.

76.original: We will await your return, then.

77.original: Should you have need of the wisdom of Ronka again, you know where to find us.

78.original: Be it a year from now or ten, we look forward to your return.

79.original: Perhaps someday we will visit your home instead.
